target: Activate the review_reminders table and expose REST + MCP interfaces to create, list, and complete decision-review reminders, giving ADHD practitioners a schedulable nudge loop for revisiting past decisions.
invariants: This packet must verify whether review_reminders exists in migration 001 or schema.sql before adding any migration.
This packet must add migration 009_review_reminders.sql only if the table is confirmed absent; if it is present, the migration step is NOT_RUN.
This packet must not modify existing decisions data or the decisions table schema.
This packet must fail-closed on unknown reminder_id (404) and unknown decision_id (400/404).
This packet must not touch files outside the allowlist.
This packet must classify unresolved ambiguity about table existence as UNKNOWN and stop.
This packet must cite DMX-CONPORT-OPTIMAL-100-migration-foundation-gate proof before relying on review_reminders from migration 001 or adding fallback SQL.

commit.message: feat(conport): add review-reminders REST routes and MCP tools

pr.title: feat(conport): review-reminders REST routes + MCP tools
pr.body: Activates the review_reminders table (adds migration 009_review_reminders.sql only if the table is absent from migration 001/schema). Adds POST /api/decisions/{id}/reminders, GET /api/reminders?workspace_id=, and POST /api/reminders/{id}/complete REST routes in enhanced_server.py. Adds create_review_reminder, list_review_reminders, and complete_review_reminder MCP tools in server.py and JSON-RPC handlers in conport_mcp_stdio.py.

steps.task: Preflight: create a fresh dedicated worktree from origin/main. Verify repo marker, origin identity, branch, and clean baseline. Inspect docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/schema.sql and all migration files under migrations/ to determine whether a review_reminders table is already defined. Record finding (EXISTS / ABSENT / UNKNOWN) in proof.
validation: Worktree path, branch, origin, marker verified and recorded in proof.
Table existence classified as EXISTS, ABSENT, or UNKNOWN — not assumed.
Proof references DMX-CONPORT-OPTIMAL-100-migration-foundation-gate outcome before this packet proceeds.

steps.task: If S1 found the review_reminders table ABSENT, create docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/migrations/009_review_reminders.sql with the table definition: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, decision_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES decisions(id), workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL, remind_at TEXT NOT NULL, completed_at TEXT, notes TEXT, created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. If EXISTS, skip and record NOT_RUN.
validation: Migration file created only when table was confirmed absent in S1.
SQL is idempotent (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS).
If table already existed, step is recorded as NOT_RUN with reason.

steps.task: Write failing tests in docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/tests/test_review_reminders.py covering: (a) POST /api/decisions/{id}/reminders creates a reminder and returns 201 with id; (b) GET /api/reminders?workspace_id= lists all non-completed reminders for the workspace; (c) POST /api/reminders/{id}/complete marks the reminder completed and sets completed_at; (d) POST on unknown decision_id returns 400 or 404; (e) complete on unknown reminder_id returns 404.
validation: All five test cases exist and fail (red) before production code is added.
Tests are self-contained and use the in-process test client.

steps.task: Implement the three REST routes in enhanced_server.py: POST /api/decisions/{decision_id}/reminders (body: remind_at required, notes optional, workspace_id required), GET /api/reminders (query param: workspace_id required, returns non-completed reminders ordered by remind_at), POST /api/reminders/{reminder_id}/complete (sets completed_at to now). Each route validates inputs and fails-closed on missing or invalid data.
validation: All five tests from S3 pass (green).
Listing endpoint returns only non-completed reminders.
No regression in other enhanced_server.py routes.

steps.task: Add three MCP tools in server.py (create_review_reminder, list_review_reminders, complete_review_reminder) with schemas mirroring the REST routes. Add corresponding JSON-RPC handlers in conport_mcp_stdio.py following the existing handler pattern.
validation: All three tools appear in the MCP tool listing.
JSON-RPC create/list/complete round-trip succeeds against a live or test instance.
Pattern consistency with existing MCP tools confirmed by code review step.
